obese individuals have a higher prevalence of sleep disorders, and that sleep disorders in turn may be a contributing factor in the development of obesity.

obesity is a multifactorial disease with a strong genetic component and a complex pathogenesis, and that the most effective treatment is lifestyle changes, with a diet low in energy and fat, and increased physical activity.
obesity is associated with a number of mental health problems, but the direction of the causal relationship is not yet clear.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
obesity is an independent risk factor for the development of sleep disorders and that sleep disorders are an independent risk factor of obesity development.
obesity and sleep disorders are closely related.
obesity is a risk factor for sleep disorders and sleep disorders are a risk factor for obesity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the prevalence of sleep apnea and other sleep disorders among patients with obesity and metabolic syndrome is much higher than previously thought.
the mental state of patients with obesity and concomitant sleep apnea syndrome is characterized by a higher frequency of depressive disorders, neurosis, and personality disorders.
the mental state of patients with obesity is not as stable as it might appear at first glance.
